instructions: These tools read one Controlvar instance (feature flags and A/B experiments) as the user whose API key this server holds. They change no flag, experiment or setting; evaluate_feature_flag records one evaluation, as an SDK call does. Flags are named by their key; experiments by the id that list_experiments gives.

tools.name: list_feature_flags
tools.title: List feature flags
tools.description: Lists the feature flags on the Controlvar instance. Each item has its `key`, `name`, `status` (ACTIVE, INACTIVE or ARCHIVED), `value_type`, `rollout_percentage`, `tags`, `updated_at`, `stale` and `stale_reasons`, and the answer has `stale_days` and `evaluations_seen`. `stale` is true when the flag looks ready to remove, and `stale_reasons` says why (not_evaluated, on_for_everyone, off_for_everyone); this is advice only, and nothing is archived or changed. `stale_days` is the number of days those reasons look back, and `evaluations_seen` is false when the instance recorded no flag evaluation in that time, so not_evaluated is not reported. `search` matches part of a flag's name or key; `status` keeps one status; `stale` keeps the stale flags (true) or the others (false). Returns at most `limit` flags (default 50, at most 100) and `total`, the number that match. When `total` is larger, call again with `skip`. The list is ordered by creation time, oldest first, so paging with `skip` reads each flag once unless flags are created or deleted meanwhile; to read one flag by its key, use get_feature_flag.

search.description: Part of a flag's name or key, 1 to 100 characters.

stale.description: true returns only stale flags, false the rest; omit for all. Archived flags are never stale.

limit.description: How many to return, from 1 to 100. Default 50.

skip.description: How many to skip, to read the next page. Default 0.

tools.name: get_feature_flag
tools.title: Read a feature flag
tools.description: Reads one feature flag by its key: status, rollout percentage, targeting rules, the values it serves when on and off, tags and timestamps. A flag that is not ACTIVE serves its off value to every user.

flag_key.description: The flag's key, as list_feature_flags shows it.

tools.name: evaluate_feature_flag
tools.title: Evaluate a flag for a user
tools.description: Asks the instance what a flag serves one user, the same answer an SDK gets: `enabled`, the `value` served, and `reason`. The reasons are: targeting_rule (a targeting rule matched); rollout (the rollout percentage decided); inactive (the flag is not ACTIVE); error (the rules could not be evaluated, so the flag is off). Put the user's attributes in `context`, for example {"country": "DE", "plan": "pro"}, so targeting rules can match them. Each call is recorded as one evaluation of the flag, with this user_id and context, as an SDK's is.

flag_key.description: The flag's key, as list_feature_flags shows it.

user_id.description: The user to evaluate the flag for, as your app identifies them.

context.description: The user's attributes, as a JSON object, for the flag's targeting rules.

tools.name: list_experiments
tools.title: List experiments
tools.description: Lists experiments. Each item has its `id` (which get_experiment and get_experiment_results take), `key`, `name`, `status` (draft, active, paused, completed or archived), `experiment_type`, `start_date`, `end_date` and `updated_at`. `search` matches part of a name or description, or a whole tag, but not the key; `status` keeps one status. Paging is the same as list_feature_flags: at most `limit` items, `total`, and `skip` for the next page.

search.description: Part of an experiment's name or description, or a whole tag, 1 to 100 characters.

limit.description: How many to return, from 1 to 100. Default 50.

skip.description: How many to skip, to read the next page. Default 0.

tools.name: get_experiment
tools.title: Read an experiment
tools.description: Reads one experiment by its id (from list_experiments): hypothesis, status, variants and their traffic allocation, metrics (one is primary), targeting rules and dates.

tools.name: get_experiment_results
tools.title: Read experiment results
tools.description: Reads the statistical results of an experiment that has started (a draft has none). For each metric and variant: the sample size, the conversion rate or mean, the difference from the control with its confidence interval, the p-value and whether it is significant, plus a summary and recommendation. Before stating a conclusion, check `srm` (a sample-ratio mismatch: users were not split as configured, so the comparison cannot be trusted) and `sample_size_adequate` (false: too few users yet).
